status: Design proposals, not implemented product screens
base_prompt:
Use case: ui-mockup. Create one polished, realistic desktop application screenshot for Recollect, an engineering memory product. This is a proposed design with entirely fictional demonstration data. Wide desktop landscape 16:10, preferably 1920x1200. Full screenshot straight-on, no device frame, no browser chrome, no perspective, no marketing hero.
Visual system inspired by Agent Memory Atlas: warm paper canvas #f7f4ec, sidebar #eee9de, surface #fffdf8, ink #101b2a, body text #2f3d4f, thin borders #d7d0c2, active sage #3d6b59 with pale sage fills, amber #e8b861 for caution. Light mode only, including sidebar. Newsreader editorial serif for page titles 38px and tasteful feature headings; Manrope 14-16px for interface and body; DM Mono 11px for uppercase eyebrow and metadata. Plenty of whitespace, tidy 8px spacing rhythm, 6px corners, almost no shadows, fine outline icons. Dark ink primary buttons, sage selection. Flat modern information design, readable crisp text, not a dashboard full of cards.
Shared shell: fixed 240px LIGHT sidebar on left, narrow topbar above main content. Recollect wordmark top left. Below, left arrow "All Brains", then a Brain switcher "Atlas Engineering" with small "TEAM BRAIN" label. Three small sidebar group labels. KNOWLEDGE: Ask, Memory, Sources, Graph. WORKSPACE: Repositories, Agents. MANAGE: Connections, Activity, Settings. All nine items must appear once in this exact order with outline icons. At bottom small circle avatar "M", text "Mike", "Workspace owner". Active page is subtly sage filled with dark sage text. Topbar breadcrumb "Atlas Engineering / {PAGE}", right "Demo workspace" badge and understated search icon. Main content has generous 40px margins. Tiny bottom-right label "Design proposal · sample data".
Avoid neon, gradients, glassmorphism, decorative blobs, oversized hero copy, dark sidebar, tiny unreadable tables, huge KPI blocks, mobile layouts. Require clear legible labels and consistent English.

views.content:
Page title "Ask your Brain", subtitle "Answers grounded in your team's knowledge." Active Ask.
Two-column layout: main conversation 70%, right evidence rail 30%. Small scope controls under heading: "All repositories", "Production", "More filters". A compact link "Search evidence" at upper right. Show one user question in a restrained paper-deep bubble: "Why did we move session storage to PostgreSQL?" Then a thoughtful assistant response on canvas, not a chat bubble: bold summary "To share sessions across replicas and simplify recovery." Body "The architecture decision cites consistent sessions, fewer moving parts, and point-in-time recovery. [1] The rollout plan records a staged migration. [2]" Under it an amber fine-bordered note "Deployment status is not confirmed by these sources." Beneath answer small inline buttons "2 sources", "Copy", "Inspect memory". Right evidence rail title "Supporting evidence" with two slim source rows "ADR 024 · Session storage" / "Decision · 14 Sep" and "Migration plan" / "Source · 18 Sep", and a text link "Open evidence".
Bottom main pinned clean composer with placeholder "Ask a question about this Brain…" and dark square arrow-send button, microcopy "Uses stored knowledge. Does not run connected tools." Below composer "This conversation is temporary." No mode dropdown visible, no model selector, no tools executing, no review queue, no fake confidence percentages. Example answer clearly qualifies recorded intent vs deployment.

views.description: Readable learned knowledge with optional correction and handovers.
views.content: Title "Memory", subtitle "What this Brain has learned, with the evidence behind it." Active Memory. Top-right understated "Add memory" button. Short inline summary "Updated automatically · Last update 4 min ago". Tabs "All", "Decisions", "Procedures", "Handovers"; All active. Search field "Find a memory…" and small filter "Needs attention · 2". Main left 65% readable list rows, not dense data grid: "Sessions use PostgreSQL" small badges "Decision" "Policy accepted" and source count 2; "Use rolling upgrades for API replicas" badges "Procedure" "Needs verification" 3 sources; "Service ownership follows the repository" badge "Convention" 1 source. First row selected. Right inspector on light surface title "Sessions use PostgreSQL", paragraph with rationale, separate compact state labels "Review: Policy accepted", "Freshness: Current", "Operational: Declared". Section "Evidence" links ADR 024 and Migration plan. Bottom optional actions "Correct", "View history", overflow menu. Show no mandatory approval queue, no Accept-all button, no long forms.

Title "Sources", subtitle "Original material your Brain can learn from." Active Sources. Dark primary "Add source" at right. Header controls simple search "Search sources…", dropdown "All collections", chips "Platform" and "Production", link "Manage views". Table with columns "Source", "Kind", "Updated", "Learning". Four readable rows: "ADR 024 · Session storage" / Document / 14 Sep / Learned; "API deployment runbook" / Document / 18 Sep / Learned; "On-call investigation" / Captured session / Today / Processing; "Infrastructure repository" / Reference only / Yesterday / Reference only. Subtle icons. Open slim right drawer "ADR 024 · Session storage" with preview paragraph, "Version 3", "Evidence retained", collection Platform, links "Version history", "Edit source", overflow. Footnote "Collections, areas, and environments organize shared evidence." No permanent retention switch in table toolbar, no mandatory Learn button per row.

Title "Graph", subtitle "Explore how your knowledge and repositories connect." Active Graph. Main content dominated by a beautiful restrained interactive network canvas taking 75% width and most height. Top single toolbar: segmented control "Knowledge" selected, "Repository", "Combined"; small search "Find an entity…"; chip "Production"; "Filters" button. Render about 12 legible nodes with fine muted edges; center sage rounded rectangle "Session service" links to "PostgreSQL", "ADR 024", "API replicas", "Migration plan", "Authentication", "Backup policy", "Platform team"; secondary smaller nodes. Use muted sage/blue/amber node markers with tiny legend "System · Evidence · Decision". Right 25% inspector heading "Session service", type System, readable supporting evidence links, "5 connections"; controls "Expand connections", "Find path", text link "Advanced analysis". Lower left small status "Current projection · 12 shown", lower right subtle fit/zoom controls. No large filters form above graph; no rebuild primary button; no enormous arbitrary graph hairball; no graph rendered as a fake deployment topology.

views.description: Repository evidence, snapshots, and environment versions.
views.content: Title "Repositories", subtitle "Published code knowledge, tied to exact revisions." Active Repositories. Tabs "Repositories" selected and "Environments". Top-right outline button "Publish from companion". Search "Find a repository…". Main table columns Repository / Published revision / Coverage / Updated. Three rows: "platform/api" / "a84b19c" / "Complete" / Today; "platform/infrastructure" / "70de239" / "Partial" / Yesterday; "platform/web" / "c42a187" / "Complete" / Today. First selected with right inspector 30% width. Inspector "platform/api", "Snapshot a84b19c", scope tags Platform and Production, compact list "Files", "Relationships", "Contributors", "Publication receipt"; note "Committed revision. Deployment is tracked separately." Under table a calm info strip "Repository publication runs on your companion. Local file paths stay on your device." Small link "Your checkouts". No Git clone control, no deploy button, no missing limitations hidden.

views.description: Connect coding tools and inspect their sessions.
views.content: Title "Agents", subtitle "Connect coding tools to this Brain." Active Agents. Dark primary button "Connect an agent". Two elegant compact horizontal setup cards for "Codex" and "Claude Code" each line "Use memory and publish supported session activity" with "Setup" link, understated line icons not detailed corporate logos. Under a divider tabs "Sessions" selected, "Capture", "Task scopes". Session list rows "Investigate session migration" / "Codex · Mike's MacBook" / "Active · Production"; "Update deployment runbook" / "Claude Code · Workstation" / "Finished · Development". Right small details pane "Capture coverage", green "Capture enabled", plain list "Supported messages", "Tool observations", amber "Some host events may be unavailable"; link "Inspect capture policy". Small bottom note "Agents select their task scope automatically. Inspect or adjust it when needed." Do not show task creation or refresh catalogue as daily primary actions. Do not suggest Recollect hosts or creates an autonomous LLM agent.

Title "Connections", subtitle "Tools this Brain can make available to authorized agents." Active Connections. Dark "Add connection" button. Tabs "Connections" selected, "Profiles", "Runners". Two to three wide clean connector rows/cards: "GitHub · Engineering" / "Available · Hosted endpoint" / "Used by: Engineering read"; "Kubernetes · Staging" / "Available · Private runner" / "Used by: Staging operations"; "Internal docs" / amber "Credentials required". Right detail surface for GitHub: endpoint metadata, "Credential source: Vault reference", status "Last successful call 6 min ago"; button "Test connection", secondary "Edit", link "View calls". Compact permissions text "Profile use, management, and sharing are separate permissions." Bottom thin callout "Only approved connectors appear in the catalogue." Show no raw secrets or broad access toggles. Connection status should distinguish configured from successfully called.

views.description: Exceptions and history, without becoming a daily work queue.
views.content: Title "Activity", subtitle "Changes, processing, and calls in this Brain." Active Activity. Tabs "Timeline" selected, "Processing", "Tool calls", "Model usage". Filter row "All activity" dropdown, "Last 7 days", subtle "Needs attention · 1" amber chip. Timeline, generous typography and thin separators: "4 min ago — 3 memories updated" small "Automatic learning · Source ADR 024"; "8 min ago — Repository snapshot published" small "platform/api · a84b19c · Mike"; amber row "12 min ago — Internal docs connection needs credentials" with "Open connection"; "21 min ago — Handover generated" small "Session migration · 4 sources"; "Yesterday — Brain access updated" small "Mike · Admin action". Right summary rail "Running in the background" with "Learning: Idle", "Graph: Current", "Capture: Receiving", and link "View processing". No large vanity KPI cards, no mandatory review tasks, no claimed merged global ordering across independent systems.

Title "Brain settings", subtitle "Set the boundaries. Let memory look after itself." Active Settings. Four compact vertically stacked settings groups visible within desktop content, using horizontal rows rather than giant cards:
"General" — "Atlas Engineering", description "Shared engineering knowledge", small "Edit".
"Access" — "6 members · Reader, writer, and admin roles", button "Manage access".
"AI & automation" — "Automatic learning: On", "Question answering: Allowed", "Model data sharing: Selected content only", "Monthly token budget: 2 million", button "Configure"; microcopy "Capture permission and model sharing are separate."
"Retention & privacy" — "Session captures: 30 days", "Documents: Until removed", link "Review policy"; microcopy "Erase removes controlled content and its dependent copies."
Right slim contextual help column "You stay in control" with sentence "Set providers, content permissions, access, and retention once. Review exceptions in Activity." Bottom separated discreet "Archive Brain" outline button. No dark mode switch, no live API keys, no destructive red wall, no multiple giant editable JSON forms. This is illustrative policy data.

This is a GLOBAL workspace screen: replace Brain shell sidebar navigation with wordmark, small WORKSPACE label then exactly "Brains", "Team", "Devices". Brains active. Remove All Brains link and Brain switcher. Bottom Mike owner avatar. Breadcrumb "Workspace / Brains". Title "Your Brains", subtitle "Separate spaces for the knowledge you work with." Dark button "Create Brain". Search "Find a Brain…" and scope chips "All", "Personal", "Shared". 3 calm roomy rows or cards with serif names: "Atlas Engineering" / "Platform decisions, code, and operating knowledge." / "Shared · 6 members"; "Personal" / "Notes and working context." / "Only you"; "Infrastructure" / "Systems, environments, and runbooks." / "Shared · 3 members". Small metadata "Updated 4 min ago" and restrained arrow to open each. Small bottom installation strip "All services connected" link "Diagnostics". No huge statistics dashboard or large setup controls.

views.description: Installation accounts, distinct from Brain permissions.
views.content: GLOBAL workspace screen: sidebar wordmark, WORKSPACE label then exactly Brains, Team, Devices, Team active. No Brain switcher/All Brains. Bottom Mike owner avatar. Breadcrumb "Workspace / Team". Title "Team", subtitle "Who can sign in to this installation." Dark "Invite teammate" button. Tabs "Members" selected, "Invitations". Restrained table columns "Person", "Sign-in", "Status", "" with rows "Mike" / "Local account" / "Owner"; "Alex Morgan" / "Organization SSO" / "Enabled"; "Sam Rivera" / "Local account" / "Enabled"; "Taylor Chen" / "Invitation" / "Pending". No actual emails needed. Selected person inspector: "Alex Morgan", "Account enabled", "Access to Brains is managed in each Brain", button "View account activity", overflow "Disable account". Subtle help strip "An account allows sign-in. It does not automatically grant access to every Brain." Show no Brain roles as global account roles.

GLOBAL workspace screen: sidebar wordmark, WORKSPACE label with exactly Brains, Team, Devices, Devices active. No Brain switcher/All Brains. Bottom Mike owner avatar. Breadcrumb "Workspace / Devices". Title "Your devices", subtitle "Companions paired to your account." Top-right outline "Pair a device". Two clean device rows: "Mike's MacBook" / "macOS · Last seen just now" / "Paired" / overflow; "Engineering workstation" / "Linux · Last seen yesterday" / "Paired" / overflow. Right light panel "How pairing works" with three short numbered steps "Run the companion", "Open the pairing link", "Approve this device". Under device list separated pale-amber pending card "Pairing request" / "New workstation · Code 4F8A2C91" / buttons "Approve" and "Decline", microcopy "Approve only the device you are pairing." Small footer "Revoking a device removes its Recollect access. Your Brain data stays." No terminal scripts or secret values displayed in the main screen.
